headline: Roukaya Ibrahim sees Brent crude trading in a wide $70–$95/bbl band for remainder of the year, with geopolitics setting both floor and ceiling
reasoning: Ibrahim argues that oil prices have a geopolitical floor around $70/bbl because falling to that level incentivises the US to escalate tensions in the Middle East, while prices rising too high (above ~$95/bbl or when US retail gasoline exceeds $4/gallon) create political pressure to de-escalate ahead of midterm elections. The fundamental backdrop is also deteriorating, which she says reinforces the $70 floor. She does not expect prices to sustainably fall below $70 for the rest of the year but equally sees de-escalation risk capping the upside. The net result is a wide trading range rather than a directional trend.
quote: Really, from a geopolitical political perspective, as well as from a fundamental perspective, there's a floor for crude oil prices in the sense that when prices, you know, reach too high of a level, that's an incentive for the US to deescalate ahead of the midterm election. And when they reach to local level, as we saw a month or so ago, around $70 a barrel for Brent, that's an incentive for them to escalate, because ultimately the situation in the Middle East has not been resolved... I think what we're likely to see for the remainder of this year is that oil is going to be in a wide trading band... with prices probably between $70 a barrel and upwards of $95 a barrel for the remainder of the year for grants.
episode_title: Is $70 oil now a floor, not a ceiling?

headline: Roukaya Ibrahim sees near-term headwinds for gold from rising real rates but maintains a favourable structural long-term outlook driven by central bank demand
reasoning: Ibrahim notes that the inverse relationship between gold and US real rates has been re-established since the start of the year, after breaking down for several years. This creates a near-term headwind as Fed rate-hike expectations in response to inflation weigh on gold. However, she maintains a structurally positive long-term view because of persistent central bank demand, with the PBoC potentially using any price weakness to accumulate gold reserves more aggressively.
quote: What we've actually seen since the beginning of this year is the inverse relationship between gold prices and US real rates has been reestablished. And that's actually a change from the prior few years when that relationship completely broke down. So I think, you know, that has really created a headwind to gold prices over the past few months, whereby, you know, expectations of a fed response to the inflation risk has created a headwind for gold prices over the near term... But ultimately, I think gold enjoys a favorable structural outlook because I think that, you know, there's still that structural demand from central banks, which in some cases might actually take advantage of the lower gold prices to accumulate their inventory, accumulate gold more aggressively in the reserve. headline: BCA Research sees S&P 500 generating positive returns through year-end driven by earnings growth, even as multiples face pressure

quote: I think this is a dyed in the wool central banker. As good as it gets. I struggle for what the new great news is. headline: BCA Research neutral on US financials despite solid Q2 earnings beat, flagging cyclicality of capital markets revenue

quote: So first of all, thank you very much for having me. Good morning. Uh, here it's good evening. Um, from from the big banks.
